FORECAST AND WARNING CRITIQUE

Genesis

The  genesis  of Dorian was  not very  well  forecast.  The  disturbance  from  which Dorian
developed  was first introduced  in  the  Tropical  Weather  Outlook with  a  low  probability  (<40%)  of
formation  within 48  h  only 18 h  prior  to  genesis. The  probabilities  were  raised  to  the  medium
category (40%–60%) in both the 2-day and 5-day periods only 12 h before Dorian formed. (Table
4).  The  poor  genesis  forecasts  were likely due  to  the  small  size  of  the  incipient  disturbance  and
the abundance of very dry mid-level air (relative humidity values <50%) surrounding the cyclone.
The  ECMWF global model  did  not  even  have a  hint  of  genesis  48  h in  advance; the  GFS model
showed genesis, but much farther east than where it actually occurred.

Track

A verification of NHC official track forecasts for Dorian is given in Table 5a. Official forecast
track errors were lower than the mean official errors for the previous 5-yr period.  A homogeneous
comparison  of  the  official  track  errors  with  selected  guidance  models  is  given in  Table  5b.
Although  the average NHC  official  track  forecast errors were  quite  low,  some  models  performed
much  better  than  NHC  at some  time  periods.  The  TVDG  consensus  model, which  doubles the
weight of three global models (GFS, ECMWF and UK) and places less weight on the solutions of
the  HWRF  and  HMON  models, performed better  than  the  official forecast  as  well  as  the other
guidance at all times.

It is  interesting  to  point  out  that  during  the  early  stages  of  Dorian, while it  was located  in
the  southeastern  Caribbean  Sea,  the  re-formation  of  the  center  after crossing  St.  Lucia  resulted
in  a  significant  shift  in  track.  Prior  to  crossing  St.  Lucia,  most  of  the  models incorrectly brought
Dorian’s center over eastern Hispaniola, and the cyclone instead moved east of Puerto Rico (Fig.
15).  These  errors  resulted  in the  lack  of  adequate  warning  for  some  of  the  islands  of  the
northeastern Caribbean Sea and also a low bias for the intensity forecast.

While some of the models and the official forecast indicated Dorian’s forward speed would
decrease near the Northwestern Bahamas, none of them indicated that Dorian was going to stall
there.
Several  NHC  forecasts  issued  on  28–30  August  brought  the  center of  Dorian  over  the
Florida  peninsula.  However,  subsequent  NHC  forecasts turned  Dorian northward  east  of  Florida
(Fig. 16).  This resulted in low track forecast errors during a time when many models still indicated

a  landfall  in  Florida.  This forecasted northward  turn  east of  Florida was  the  basis  for  not  issuing
a hurricane warning for Miami-Dade and Broward Counties in South Florida.

Intensity

A verification of NHC official intensity forecasts for Dorian is given in Table 6a.  The official
1- to 3-day forecast intensity errors were larger than the mean official errors for the previous 5-yr
period.  A homogeneous comparison of the official intensity errors with selected guidance models
is given in Table 6b. With the exception of the Corrected Consensus model HCCA and the Florida
State  Super  Ensemble  (FSSE), which both performed  better  than  the NHC forecast at  various
times, the  rest  of  the  models  produced  errors  larger  than  the  official  forecast.  Most  of  the  large
errors are related to the fact that Dorian’s center did not move over Hispaniola, and the failure in
forecasting rapid  intensification when Dorian was  near  the  Bahamas. It  is  important  to  note  that
none of the  intensity  models  were  able  to  capture the intensity trend of  Dorian five days  prior  to
the hurricane reaching its peak intensity of 160 kt (Fig. 17).

Tropical  Storm  and  Hurricane  wind  watches  and  warnings  associated  with  Dorian  are
given  in  Table  7. Advisories  on  Tropical  Depression  Five, which  later  became  Dorian, were
initiated at 1500 UTC 24 August when the cyclone was centered a little more than 750 n mi east-
southeast  of  Barbados. The  first  Tropical  Storm  Watch  was  then  issued by  the  government  of

9  h  later.  Watches  and  warnings  were  gradually  extended  westward  and  northwestward  across
the  eastern  Caribbean,  including  Puerto  Rico  and  adjacent  islands. A  portion  of  these  islands,
including  Puerto  Rico, were under  a  Tropical  Storm  Warning  and  a  Hurricane  Watch  since  0900
UTC  27  August,  or  33 h  before  Dorian  reached  the  area. However,  since  the  intensification  of
Dorian  occurred  sooner  than  anticipated,  the  Tropical  Storm  Warning  for  the  British  and  U.S.
Virgin  Islands  was  upgraded  to a  Hurricane Warning  while  Dorian  was  already  producing
hurricane conditions in the U.S. Virgin Islands.

The government of the Bahamas issued a Hurricane Watch for the northwestern Bahamas
at  0900  UTC  30  August, and it  was upgraded  to a Hurricane  Warning  12  h  later. The hurricane
made  its  first  landfall  in  the northwestern  Bahamas at  Elbow Cay  43  h  after  the  issuance  of  the
hurricane warning. However, tropical-storm-force winds started a few hours earlier.

Since  Dorian  took  a  track  parallel to and  not  far  from  the  southeastern U.S.  seaboard,
most  of  the United  States  East  Coast from  Florida  to  Virginia was  under  a  watch  or  warning  for
wind  and  storm  surge  as  indicated  in  Table 7  and Table 8,  respectively. Although  at  one

forecasts  shifted  offshore,  and  it  was  not necessary  to  issue a  Hurricane  Watch  or  Warning  for
Miami-Dade  or  Broward  counties  in  South  Florida.  Historically,  it has  been uncommon to issue
Hurricane  Watches  or Warnings  for  the northwestern Bahamas  and  not  issue  them  for  South
Florida, particularly for a westward-moving hurricane.

Tropical  storm  watches  and  warnings  were  also  issued  for  portions  of  southeastern
Massachusetts  and  eastern  Maine. While  the  strongest  winds  associated  with  Dorian  remained

Storm Surge Forecasts and Warnings

NHC  issued  its  first  storm  surge  forecast  for  the  Bahamas  at  1200  UTC  30  August,
anticipating  that  water  levels  would rise by  as  much  as  10  to  15  ft  above  normal  tide  levels  in
areas of onshore winds.  Once it became increasingly likely that Dorian would be a powerful major
hurricane  and  slow  down  while  near  and  over  the  northwestern  Bahamas,  the storm  surge
forecast was raised to 15 to 20 ft above normal tide levels at 0300 UTC 1 September and then 18
to 23 ft above normal tide levels at 1500 UTC 1 September, specifically for the Abaco Islands and
Grand  Bahama  Island.  While  no  gauge  measurements  are  available  from  the  hardest-hit  areas,
eyewitness accounts indicate that at least 20 ft of inundation occurred on those islands.

Due  to  Dorian’s  forecast  track parallel  to  the  southeastern  U.S.  coastline,  storm  surge
watches and warnings were in effect at various times along an extended, continuous segment of
that  coast (Table  8).  Storm  surge  warnings  ultimately  extended  from  Lantana,  Florida  (central
Palm  Beach  County),  northward  to  Poquoson, Virginia  (Fig. 18).  These  warnings  included  land
areas bordering Pamlico and Albemarle Sounds in North Carolina, as well as the southern portion
of  Chesapeake  Bay.  In  addition,  a Storm Surge Watch  was  issued,  but  never  upgraded  to  a
warning,  for  a  small  segment  of  the  Florida  coast  north  of  Deerfield  Beach  to  Lantana  (the
southern  Palm  Beach  County  coast).  Based  on  NOS  tide  gauge  and  USGS  pressure  sensor
data,  at  least  3  ft  of  inundation (which  NHC  uses  as  a  first-cut  threshold  for  the  storm  surge
watch/warning)  occurred  within  some  parts  of  the  warning  area,  particularly  portions  of
northeastern  Florida, the  Grand  Strand  of  South  Carolina, eastern  North  Carolina, and
southeastern  Virginia.  Other  portions  of  the  warning area did  not  verify,  with  inundation  being
less  than  3  ft  above  ground  level  along  the  east-central  Florida  coast,  the  Georgia  coast,  the
South  Carolina  Low Country  coast,  and  much  of  the  North  Carolina  coast  between  Cape  Fear
and Cape Lookout.

Although a sizeable portion of the Storm Surge Warning area did not verify, the issuance
of the watch and warning was justified given that a slight westward deviation of Dorian’s track, or
an expansion of its wind field, would have caused significant storm surge flooding to occur along
a larger proportion of the coast.  This dilemma is illustrated by NWS Probabilistic Storm Surge (P-
Surge)  ensemble  tracks  from  the  NHC  forecast  released  at  1500  UTC  1  September,  when  the
storm  surge  watch  was  first  issued  for  a  portion of  the  Florida  east  coast (Fig. 19). Given  typical
uncertainties in tropical cyclone track forecasts, there was the potential for Dorian to move closer
to, or even over the Florida peninsula, which would have caused significant storm surge flooding
along the  east-central  coast  of  Florida.  The  solid  black  line  in  the  figure  is  Dorian’s  actual  track,
which shows that the hurricane ultimately moved on the eastern side of the ensemble spread and
consequently lowered the threat of significant storm surge along the east-central Florida coast.

The first storm surge forecast for a portion of the U.S. east coast was issued at 1500 UTC
1 September and called for maximum inundation heights of 4 to 7 ft above ground level between
Jupiter Inlet and the Volusia/Brevard County Line in Florida.  That same inundation forecast was
extended northward along the southeastern U.S. coast, eventually reaching as far north as Cape
Lookout,  North  Carolina,  by  2100  UTC  3  September.  Forecast  inundation  amounts  were  also
increased  as  high  as  5  to  8  ft  above  ground  level  from  Isle  of  Palms  to  Myrtle  Beach  in  South
Carolina  at  0900  UTC  4  September.  Maximum  water  levels  along  the  southeastern  U.S.  coast

[PDF page 13]
Hurricane Dorian  13

south of Cape Lookout were around 4 ft above ground level, which was at the lower bound of the
storm  surge  forecast.  Because  Dorian  stayed  far  enough  offshore  to  prevent  significant  storm
surge  flooding  along  the  coast,  the  range  of forecast inundation  heights  in  that  area  ended  up
being a few feet too high.

In  eastern  North  Carolina  between  Cape  Lookout  and  Duck,  including  the  Pamlico  and
Albemarle Sounds, the initial storm surge forecasts were 3 to 5 ft above ground level at 2100 UTC
3  September.  This  forecast  was  gradually  raised  over  time,  ultimately  peaking  at  4  to  7  ft  above
ground level for the forecast issued at 1200 UTC 5 September.  The storm surge forecast for this
area  proved  to  be  accurate,  as  maximum  water  levels  of  5  to  7  ft  above  ground  level  were
observed  on  parts  of  Hatteras  Island,  and  4  to  6  ft  above  ground  level  was measured  on  other
parts  of  the  Outer  Banks  and  the  western  side  of  Pamlico  Sound.  Farther  north,  maximum
inundation  heights  of  2  to  4  ft  above  ground  level  were  forecast  north  of  Duck  to  Poquoson,
Virginia, including the Hampton Roads area.  Maximum observed water levels in that region were
2 to 3 ft above ground level.

Impact-Based Decision Support Services (IDSS) and Public Communication
NHC coordinated  extensively  with  the  meteorological  services  of  numerous  countries  in
the eastern Caribbean  Sea  beginning  on  25  August,  as  they  issued  various  tropical  storm  and
hurricane  watches  and  warnings  for  their  respective  areas  of  responsibility. Coordination  and
discussion  of  the  issuance  of  watches  and  warnings  with  the  Bahamas  Meteorological  Service
began on 29 August.

NHC  began  providing  decision  support  to  emergency  managers  on 24 August  when
Dorian  formed east  of the  Lesser  Antilles. These  initial  briefings  were  in  support  of  Puerto  Rico
and the U.S. Virgin Islands and included FEMA headquarters and FEMA Region 2. As the threat
expanded to the continental U.S., NHC briefings included FEMA Region 3, FEMA Region 4, and
the states of Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina, and Virginia. These briefings were
coordinated  through  the  FEMA  Hurricane  Liaison  Team,  embedded  at  NHC,  and  included
telephone briefings and Federal/State video-teleconferences. The coordination of information and
briefings  continued  through  September  7  when  the  impacts  associated  with  Dorian  wound  down
across the far northeastern U.S.

The Tropical Analysis and Forecast Branch of NHC provided 25 live briefings on Hurricane
Dorian to the U.S. Coast Guard Districts 7 and 8 between 26 August and 6 September, in support
of their life-saving mission.

A  limited  media  pool  was  initiated  on 27 August,  operating  from 0700–0930  EDT (1100–
1330  UTC), and  again  from 1700–1830  EDT (2100–2230  UTC).  For  three  days while the  storm
was in the Caribbean Sea and not yet a direct threat to the mainland United States, live interviews
were offered to network pool members and to South Florida media affiliates.

The media pool  was  expanded  to continuous operations on  30 August,  operating  from
0700–2330 EDT (1100–0330 UTC). A Spanish-language media pool was also initiated to address
a  high  Spanish  media  demand. With  the  threat  to  South  Florida  over  on 3 September,  a  change

[PDF page 14]
Hurricane Dorian  14

from  a  local  media  pool  to  a  network  pool  was  made.  This  provided  a  high  priority  to  networks
and  more  availability  to  those  local  stations elsewhere in  the  potential  path  of  the  storm.  In total
during  the  pool  for  Dorian, NHC provided 241  network  interviews,  124  local  station  interviews,
and  52  Spanish language  interviews  through  the  media  pool,  in  addition  to  105  generic  updates
made available to all pool members.

In addition, NHC provided 32 Facebook Live broadcasts via its Facebook page during the
11-day  span  of  the  media  pool  (0830,  1130, and 1730 EDT/1230,  1530,  2130  UTC).  NHC
experienced 6 million views, with a single peak live view of 456,000 on the 1130 EDT (1530 UTC)
1 September broadcast as Dorian neared landfall in the northwestern Bahamas.

NHC  provided  Key  Messages  in  the  Tropical  Cyclone  Discussion and in graphical format
on the NHC webpage and through social media posts from 25 August through 8 September.
NHC web pages were accessed approximately 340 million times between 24 August and
8  September  resulting  in  approximately  6.5 billion  hits.  Products  specific  to  Dorian  were  viewed
186 million times during this period, with a majority of the views going to graphical products such
as the key messages, cone graphic, and the wind speed probabilities.

**Hurricane Dorian** was an extremely powerful and catastrophic [tropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone"), which became the most intense on record to strike [the Bahamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bahamas "The Bahamas"). It is tied with the [1935 Labor Day hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1935_Labor_Day_hurricane "1935 Labor Day hurricane") and [Hurricane Melissa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Melissa "Hurricane Melissa") in 2025 for the strongest [landfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall "Landfall") in the Atlantic basin in terms of maximum sustained winds.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-1) It is regarded as the worst [natural disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_disaster "Natural disaster") in the Bahamas' recorded history.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-worstdisaster-2) With winds peaking at 185 mph (295 km/h), it was also one of the most powerful hurricanes recorded in the [Atlantic Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") in terms of [1-minute sustained winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_sustained_wind "Maximum sustained wind"), and the strongest since [Wilma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Wilma "Hurricane Wilma") in [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Atlantic_hurricane_season "2005 Atlantic hurricane season"). Dorian was the fourth [named storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Named_storm "Named storm"), second hurricane, the first [major hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_hurricane "Major hurricane"), and the first [Category 5 hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category_5_hurricane "Category 5 hurricane") of the [2019 Atlantic hurricane season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Atlantic_hurricane_season "2019 Atlantic hurricane season"). Dorian struck the [Abaco Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abaco_Islands "Abaco Islands") on September 1 with maximum sustained winds of 185 mph (295 km/h), tying with the [1935 Labor Day hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1935_Labor_Day_hurricane "1935 Labor Day hurricane") and Melissa for the highest wind speeds of an Atlantic hurricane ever recorded at landfall. Dorian went on to strike [Grand Bahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Bahama "Grand Bahama") at similar intensity, stalling just north of the territory with unrelenting winds for at least 24 hours. The resultant damage to these islands was catastrophic; most structures were flattened or swept to sea, and at least 70,000 people were left homeless. After it ravaged through The Bahamas, Dorian proceeded along the coasts of the [Southeastern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_United_States "Southeastern United States") and [Atlantic Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Canada "Atlantic Canada"), leaving behind considerable damage and economic losses in those regions.

Dorian developed from a [tropical wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_wave "Tropical wave") on August 24 over the Central Atlantic. The storm moved through the [Lesser Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_Antilles "Lesser Antilles") and became a hurricane north of the [Greater Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Antilles "Greater Antilles") on August 28. Dorian proceeded to undergo [rapid intensification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_intensification "Rapid intensification") over the following days, before reaching its peak as a [Category 5 hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffir%E2%80%93Simpson_scale#Category_5 "Saffir–Simpson scale") with [one-minute sustained winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_sustained_winds "Maximum sustained winds") of 185 mph (295 km/h) and a minimum central pressure of 910 millibars (26.87 inHg) by September 1. It made landfall in The Bahamas in [Elbow Cay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elbow_Cay "Elbow Cay"), just east of Abaco Island, and again on [Grand Bahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Bahama "Grand Bahama") several hours later, where it remained nearly stationary for the next day or so. After weakening considerably, Dorian began moving northwestward on September 3, parallel to the east coast of [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida"). Dwindling in strength, the hurricane turned to the northeast the next day and made landfall on [Cape Hatteras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Hatteras "Cape Hatteras") ([North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina")) at Category 2 intensity on September 6. Dorian transitioned into an extratropical cyclone on September 7, before striking first [Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Scotia "Nova Scotia") and then [Newfoundland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newfoundland "Newfoundland") with hurricane-force winds on the next day. The storm finally dissipated near [Greenland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenland "Greenland") on September 10.

From August 26 to August 28, the storm affected several parts of the northernmost Lesser Antilles. Damaging winds primarily affected the [Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Islands "Virgin Islands") where gusts reached 111 mph (179 km/h). Extensive precautionary measures were taken to mitigate damage, especially in [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"), where one person died. Elsewhere in the Lesser Antilles, impacts from the storm were relatively minor. In preparation for the storm, the states of Florida, [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)"), [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina"), [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina") and [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia") all declared a [state of emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency") and many coastal counties from Florida to North Carolina issued mandatory evacuation orders. Damage in The Bahamas was catastrophic due to the prolonged and intense storm conditions, including heavy rainfall, high winds and [storm surge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storm_surge "Storm surge"), with thousands of homes destroyed and at least 77 direct deaths recorded, 74 of which occurred in The Bahamas. The true death toll is unknown, with 245 people still missing as of August 2020.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-3) Dorian is the costliest disaster in Bahamian history, estimated to have left behind $3.4 billion (2020 USD) in damage in that country, while causing a total of $5.08 billion in damage overall. Due to the damage and loss of life, the name Dorian was later retired from the Atlantic rotating naming lists by the [World Meteorological Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Meteorological_Organization "World Meteorological Organization").

On August 19, 2019, the [National Hurricane Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hurricane_Center "National Hurricane Center") (NHC) identified a [tropical wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_wave "Tropical wave")—an elongated [trough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trough_(meteorology) "Trough (meteorology)") of [low air pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-pressure_area "Low-pressure area")—within a [monsoon trough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon_trough "Monsoon trough") over [Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinea "Guinea") and [Senegal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senegal "Senegal") in western Africa. [Convective activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmospheric_convection "Atmospheric convection") associated with the wave was limited by an abundance of [Saharan dust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineral_dust#Saharan_dust "Mineral dust") in the region.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-4) Propagating west over the tropical Atlantic Ocean, the system remained disorganized for several days.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-5) On August 23, a defined area of low pressure consolidated at the surface and thunderstorm activity increased.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-6) The system acquired sufficient organized convection to be classified as Tropical Depression Five at 15:00 UTC on August 24. At this time the system was situated 805 mi (1,300 km) east-southeast of [Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados "Barbados"). A deep [ridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridge_(meteorology) "Ridge (meteorology)") imparted continued westward movement of the depression, steering it toward the [Lesser Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_Antilles "Lesser Antilles").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-7) A small cyclone, it soon developed a defined inner core with a 12 mi (18 km) wide [eye-like](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_(cyclone) "Eye (cyclone)") feature. This marked the system's intensification into a tropical storm, at which time it was [assigned the name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_naming "Tropical cyclone naming")_Dorian_ by the NHC.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-8) Thereafter, moderate [wind shear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_shear "Wind shear") and surrounding dry air limited further organization.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-9)[Rainbands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainbands "Rainbands") gradually wrapped more around Dorian on August 25–26, though convection remained inconsistent.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-11)

Dorian continued moving west and made landfall at 01:00 UTC on August 27 in Barbados, bringing tropical storm-force winds and heavy rain.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-14) It then started moving northwestward toward [Saint Lucia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Lucia "Saint Lucia"). At 11:00 UTC of the same day, Dorian made landfall on the island of Saint Lucia as a tropical storm,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-TCR-15) briefly disrupting the core of the storm, before entering the [Caribbean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-16) The storm underwent a center relocation further north, to the west of [Martinique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martinique "Martinique"), causing the island to experience tropical storm-force winds as well.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-17) Dorian had been predicted to travel northwest and pass over or near the [Dominican Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Republic "Dominican Republic") or [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-18) possibly allowing their mountainous terrain to weaken the tropical storm. At that time, dry air and wind shear were expected to prevent Dorian from attaining hurricane status—although just barely.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-19) However, Dorian took a more northerly track than expected, causing it to pass to the east of Puerto Rico and hit the [US Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Virgin_Islands "US Virgin Islands"). On August 28, Dorian intensified into a [Category 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffir%E2%80%93Simpson_scale#Category_1 "Saffir–Simpson scale") hurricane as it approached the US Virgin Islands, where hurricane-force winds were recorded; at 15:30 UTC that day, Dorian became a hurricane and made landfall in Saint Croix and a few hours later, at 18:00 UTC, Dorian made landfall on Saint Thomas at a slightly higher intensity.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-TCR-15)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-CBC_1-20) However, the hurricane's small size prevented mainland Puerto Rico from experiencing hurricane- or tropical storm-force winds, although this was not the case for the [Spanish Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Virgin_Islands "Spanish Virgin Islands").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-21)

Once the system moved north past the Virgin Islands, the storm entered a more favorable environment. On the next day, the system started to [rapidly intensify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_intensification "Rapid intensification"), reaching Category 2 status early on August 30.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-22) Rapid intensification continued, and the storm eventually reached major hurricane status several hours later, on the same day.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-23) This strengthening trend came to a halt for the remainder of the day, but soon resumed.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-24) The system continued strengthening, and on August 31, Dorian attained Category 4 major hurricane status.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-25) Dorian reached Category 5 intensity on the following day.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-26) On the morning of September 1, a [dropsonde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dropsonde "Dropsonde") deployed by [a NOAA aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOAA_Hurricane_Hunters "NOAA Hurricane Hunters") measured a wind gust of 176 knots (326 km/h; 203 mph) at the surface. With one-minute sustained winds of 180 mph (285 km/h) and a minimum pressure of 913 mbar (27.0 inHg), the NHC noted that Dorian was the strongest hurricane in modern records to affect the northwestern Bahamas.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-NHC_01/09/2019-27)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Dorian_2019-09-02_1548Z.jpg/250px-Dorian_2019-09-02_1548Z.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dorian_2019-09-02_1548Z.jpg)

Hurricane Dorian as seen from the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") on September 2, 2019

At 16:40 UTC on September 1, Dorian made landfall on [Great Abaco Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abaco_Islands "Abaco Islands") in The Bahamas, with one-minute sustained winds of 185 mph (298 km/h), wind gusts over 220 mph (355 km/h), and a central barometric pressure of 910 millibars (27 inHg),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-29) as Dorian reached its peak intensity during landfall.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Discussion_Number_34-30) Storm chaser [Josh Morgerman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Morgerman "Josh Morgerman") observed a pressure of 913.4 mbar (26.97 inHg) in [Marsh Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsh_Harbour "Marsh Harbour").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-31) Dorian's forward speed decreased around this time, slowing to a westward crawl of 5 mph (8.0 km/h).[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Discussion_Number_34-30) At 02:00 UTC on September 2, Dorian made landfall on [Grand Bahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Bahama "Grand Bahama") near the same intensity, with the same sustained wind speed.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-32) Afterward, Dorian's forward speed slowed to just 1 knot (1.2 mph; 1.9 km/h), as the [Bermuda High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bermuda_High "Bermuda High") that was steering the storm westward weakened. Later that day, the storm began to undergo an [eyewall replacement cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyewall_replacement_cycle "Eyewall replacement cycle") to the north of Grand Bahama; the Bermuda High to the northeast of Dorian also collapsed, causing Dorian to stall just north of Grand Bahama.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-34) Around the same time, the combination of the eyewall replacement cycle and [upwelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upwelling "Upwelling") of cold water caused Dorian to begin weakening, with Dorian dropping to Category 4 status at 15:00 UTC.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-35) Due to the absence of steering currents, Dorian stalled north of Grand Bahama for about a day.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Discussion_Number_41-37) Dorian subsequently weakened to a Category 2 storm on September 3, before beginning to move northwestward at 15:00 UTC, parallel to the east coast of Florida, with Dorian's wind field expanding during this time.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Discussion_Number_41-37)

While moving northwestward, Dorian gradually reorganized. At 06:00 UTC on September 5, Dorian moved over the warm waters of the [Gulf Stream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Stream "Gulf Stream") and completed its eyewall replacement cycle, reintensifying into a Category 3 hurricane off the coast of [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-38) However, several hours later, Dorian encountered high [wind shear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_shear "Wind shear"), causing the storm to weaken to a Category 2 hurricane[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-39) early on September 6.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-40) Then, at 12:35 UTC that day, Dorian made landfall in [Cape Hatteras, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Hatteras,_North_Carolina "Cape Hatteras, North Carolina") as a Category 2 hurricane, with 1-minute sustained winds of 100 mph (160 km/h) and a minimum central pressure of 956 mb (28.2 inHg).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-TCR-15)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-41) Afterward, Dorian began to transition into an [extratropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extratropical_cyclone "Extratropical cyclone") as it quickly moved northeastward, completing its transition on September 7.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-42) The storm maintained its intensity, due to baroclinic processes, generating Category 2 hurricane-equivalent winds.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-44) Several hours later, at 7:05 p.m. [AST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Time_Zone "Atlantic Time Zone") on September 7 (23:05 UTC on September 7), Dorian made landfall on [Sambro Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sambro_Creek,_Nova_Scotia "Sambro Creek, Nova Scotia"), [Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Scotia "Nova Scotia"), as a Category 1-equivalent [extratropical storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extratropical_cyclone "Extratropical cyclone"),[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-45) before making its fourth and final landfall on the northern part of [Newfoundland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newfoundland_(island) "Newfoundland (island)") several hours later.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-TCR-15)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-46) By 11:00 p.m. AST on September 8 (03:00 UTC on September 9), Dorian had moved into the [Labrador Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labrador_Sea "Labrador Sea"), 375 miles off the coast, moving northeastward at 24 mph (39 km/h), with wind speeds of 60 mph (97 km/h), maintaining [tropical storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_storm "Tropical storm")-strength winds.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-47) As Dorian no longer posed a threat to Atlantic Canada at that time, the NHC issued their final advisory on the storm.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-48) On September 10, Dorian's extratropical remnant dissipated off the coast of southern [Greenland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenland "Greenland").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-49)

With sustained winds of 185 mph (295 km/h), Dorian is the strongest hurricane on record to strike The Bahamas since records began in 1851.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-KRecord-53)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-NHC_01/09/2019-27)

Dorian is tied with the [1935 Labor Day hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1935_Labor_Day_hurricane "1935 Labor Day hurricane") and [Hurricane Melissa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Melissa "Hurricane Melissa") in 2025 for the highest sustained winds at landfall in an Atlantic hurricane;[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-54) by the same metric, it is also the strongest Atlantic hurricane since [Wilma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Wilma "Hurricane Wilma") in 2005. By central pressure, it was the fifth lowest pressure of a hurricane at landfall. Dorian is one of only two Category 5 hurricanes to make landfall on the [Abaco Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abaco_Islands "Abaco Islands"), the other having occurred in [1932](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1932_Bahamas_hurricane "1932 Bahamas hurricane"),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-MSNAbaco-55) and is the only such storm on record to have impacted [Grand Bahama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Bahama "Grand Bahama").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-KGrandBahama-56) With Dorian, 2019 became the fourth consecutive year to produce at least one Category 5 hurricane in the North Atlantic.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-C5-57)[[nb 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-58)

Additionally, Dorian featured the highest sustained winds in an Atlantic hurricane recorded at latitude (26.6°N),[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-KLatitude-59) and was the strongest Atlantic-basin hurricane ever detected outside of the [tropics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Atlantic "Tropical Atlantic"), surpassing [Hurricane Irma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Irma "Hurricane Irma").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-COLOSTATE_Dorian_records-60) Dorian also tracked the least distance in a 24-hour period recorded for an Atlantic major hurricane since [Hurricane Betsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Betsy "Hurricane Betsy") in [1965](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_Atlantic_hurricane_season "1965 Atlantic hurricane season").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-COLOSTATE_Dorian_records-60) The storm impacted a single land area as a Category 5 hurricane for the longest duration recorded in the Atlantic basin, with portions of Dorian's eyewall striking Great Abaco Island and Grand Bahama with Category 5 winds for about 22 hours.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-strongest,_slowest_hurricane-61)

## Preparations

### Caribbean

Main article: [Effects of Hurricane Dorian in the Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effects_of_Hurricane_Dorian_in_the_Caribbean "Effects of Hurricane Dorian in the Caribbean")

Prior to Dorian's arrival in the Lesser Antilles, local governments issued various [tropical cyclone warnings and watches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_warnings_and_watches "Tropical cyclone warnings and watches") across the islands.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-TCR-15)[LIAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LIAT "LIAT") cancelled multiple flights across the Lesser Antilles due to the storm and airports across the [Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Islands "Virgin Islands") temporarily suspended operations.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-STS_1-62)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-63) Many of the threatened islands suffered devastating impacts in 2017 from Hurricanes [Irma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Irma "Hurricane Irma") and [Maria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Maria "Hurricane Maria"), lending to greater vigilance.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Vigil-64) In Barbados, thirty-eight shelters opened island-wide, with 103 residents seeking refuge in them. All public services were suspended for the duration of the storm.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-BT_1-65)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-BT_2-66) Homeless persons were transported to shelter by emergency personnel.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-67) On August 26, St. Lucia prime minister [Allen Chastanet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Chastanet "Allen Chastanet") announced that the nation would "shut down" for the duration of Dorian.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-68) In Dominica, Prime Minister [Roosevelt Skerrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roosevelt_Skerrit "Roosevelt Skerrit") ordered all public sector workers to remain home and prepare for the storm.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-69) The Ministry of Public Works mobilized heavy machinery and the police were placed on high alert.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Vigil-64)

Puerto Rico [Wanda Vázquez Garced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanda_V%C3%A1zquez_Garced "Wanda Vázquez Garced") declared a [state of emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency") for the territory on August 27.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-CBC_1-20) The following day, the [Puerto Rico National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico_National_Guard "Puerto Rico National Guard") was activated to support any relief operations related to the storm.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-70) Fears centered around the still-unstable power grid which was largely destroyed by Maria;[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-nyt826-71) hundreds of utility workers were deployed to quickly fix any outages.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-WP_0828-72) In some areas, power lines remained affixed to palm trees.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-nyt826-71) An estimated 30,000 homes still had damaged roofs from the 2017 hurricane.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-73) Territory-wide, 360 shelters with a collective capacity of 48,500 persons opened; 24,000 cots were distributed to these shelters.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-CBC_1-20) A state of emergency was declared for the [United States Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Virgin_Islands "United States Virgin Islands") on August 28.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-CBC_1-20) Curfews were enacted for the British and United States Virgin Islands for the duration of the hurricane.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-STS_1-62)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-VINO_0828-74)

### Bahamas

Main article: [Effects of Hurricane Dorian in The Bahamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effects_of_Hurricane_Dorian_in_The_Bahamas "Effects of Hurricane Dorian in The Bahamas")

A warning to take immediate cover was issued by the NHC Twitter account, at 11 a.m. [EDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on September 1, 2019, as Dorian made landfall in [Elbow Cay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elbow_Cay "Elbow Cay"), [Bahamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bahamas "The Bahamas"), at 16:40 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC "UTC") as a Category 5 hurricane.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-75)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-76) Samuel Butler, the [Royal Bahamas Police Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Bahamas_Police_Force "Royal Bahamas Police Force") assistant commissioner with responsibility for Grand Bahama and the Northern Region (Abaco, Bimini and the Berry Islands), told residents "if you do not heed to the warning [...] we know that the end could be fatal" and Don Cornish, the administrator with the City of [Freeport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeport,_Bahamas "Freeport, Bahamas") told others seeking shelter at Old Bahama Bay Hotel "that is not a good idea [...] reconsider that decision".[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-77)

#### Florida

On August 28, Florida governor [Ron DeSantis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_DeSantis "Ron DeSantis") declared a state of emergency for 26 counties in the hurricane's expected path.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-WP_0828-72)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-78) This later expanded to the entire state on August 29. First responders distributed sandbags in many counties. Residents began stocking up on supplies throughout the state. In [Brevard County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brevard_County,_Florida "Brevard County, Florida"), locals worked to trim large tree branches to protect power lines.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-79) The [University of Central Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida "University of Central Florida"), [Stetson University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stetson_University "Stetson University"), [Rollins College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rollins_College "Rollins College"), and [Daytona State College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daytona_State_College "Daytona State College") cancelled classes between August 30 and September 3.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-80) In addition, the [Florida Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Institute_of_Technology "Florida Institute of Technology"), [University of North Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_North_Florida "University of North Florida"), [Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embry-Riddle_Aeronautical_University "Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University"), [Florida Atlantic University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Atlantic_University "Florida Atlantic University"), [University of South Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_South_Florida "University of South Florida"), [Florida International University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_International_University "Florida International University") and the [University of Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Miami "University of Miami") cancelled classes for at least one day on top of the three-day Labor Day weekend.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The [National Park Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Park_Service "National Park Service") shut down [Biscayne National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biscayne_National_Park "Biscayne National Park") starting at 1:30pm on August 30.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-81)

When it became apparent that Dorian would near the Florida coastline, a tropical storm watch was issued for the Florida east coast from [Deerfield Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deerfield_Beach,_Florida "Deerfield Beach, Florida") to [Sebastian Inlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Inlet "Sebastian Inlet") on August 31. It was upgraded to a tropical storm warning a few hours later. A hurricane watch was issued for the area north of Deerfield Beach on September 1, and it was upgraded to a hurricane warning later that day. On the night of September 1, a hurricane watch was issued for [Volusia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volusia_County,_Florida "Volusia County, Florida") and [Broward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broward_County,_Florida "Broward County, Florida") counties, which was later upgraded to a hurricane warning and extended down the coast.

The [Florida State League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_League "Florida State League") and [Gulf Coast League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Coast_League "Gulf Coast League") of [Minor League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minor_League_Baseball "Minor League Baseball") both cancelled the remainder of the regular season and the playoffs due to the hurricane.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-82)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-83) In college football, the game between the [Florida State Seminoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Seminoles_football "Florida State Seminoles football") and the [Boise State Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boise_State_Broncos_football "Boise State Broncos football") originally scheduled for 7 p.m. on August 31 in Jacksonville was moved to 12:00 p.m. on August 31 in Tallahassee to move the game out of the path of the storm.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-84) The [Orlando Pride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Pride "Orlando Pride") of the [National Women's Soccer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Women's_Soccer_League "National Women's Soccer League") postponed their game against the [Washington Spirit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Spirit "Washington Spirit") from August 31 to October 5.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-85) The [Tampa Bay Rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Rays "Tampa Bay Rays") of [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball") also postponed a game against the [Baltimore Orioles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Orioles "Baltimore Orioles").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-86)

[Kay Ivey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kay_Ivey "Kay Ivey"), [Governor of Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Alabama "Governor of Alabama"), announced that the [Alabama National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_National_Guard "Alabama National Guard") would be sending up to fifty support personnel to Florida to aid in recovery efforts.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-87)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-88) On September 1, Governor DeSantis said that 4,500 members of the [United States National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_National_Guard "United States National Guard") had been activated to help aid those affected by Dorian, saying that the hurricane is "way too close for comfort."[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-89) On Sunday, September 1, [Jacksonville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville,_Florida "Jacksonville, Florida"), Florida, announced mandatory evacuations for Monday, September 2, taking effect at 8 a.m. The city bridges closed when wind speeds of 40 mph (64 km/h) were recorded. Emergency shelters opened at 10 a.m. on Monday.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Jacksonville_evacuation-90)[Broward County Public Schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broward_County_Public_Schools "Broward County Public Schools") will be closed Tuesday;[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-91) all city and government offices, as well as all [Duval County Public Schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duval_County_Public_Schools "Duval County Public Schools"), [St. Johns County Public Schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Johns_County,_Florida "St. Johns County, Florida"), and [Brevard Public Schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brevard_Public_Schools "Brevard Public Schools") will be closed for Tuesday and Wednesday. Florida"), and [Atlantic Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Beach,_Florida "Atlantic Beach, Florida") will closed Sunday notice.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-92)[Legoland Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legoland_Florida "Legoland Florida") and parts of [Walt Disney [Wi-Fi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wi-Fi "Wi-Fi") to everyone in Florida, [Verizon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verizon "Verizon") provided unlimited calling, data, and texting for customers, and [AT&T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AT&T "AT&T") waived data overage charges for residents.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-97) On September 3, 115 general shelters and 48 special needs shelters were open across the state of Florida.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-98)

emergency for coastal counties of Georgia that are in the forecast path of the hurricane, including [Brantley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brantley_County,_Georgia "Brantley County, Georgia"), [Bryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_County,_Georgia "Bryan County, Georgia"), [Camden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camden_County,_Georgia "Camden County, Georgia"), [Charlton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlton_County,_Georgia "Charlton County, Georgia"), [Chatham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatham_County,_Georgia "Chatham County, Georgia"), [Effingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effingham_County,_Georgia "Effingham County, Georgia"), [Glynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glynn_County,_Georgia "Glynn County, Georgia"), [Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_County,_Georgia "Liberty County, Georgia"), [Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_County,_Georgia "Long County, Georgia"), On August 31, [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina") governor [Henry McMaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_McMaster "Henry McMaster") declared a state of emergency for the entire state after the path of Dorian shifted to affect South Carolina as a strong hurricane.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-106)

On September 1, during a news conference, Governor McMaster announced that mandatory evacuations for [Jasper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasper_County,_South_Carolina "Jasper County, South Carolina"), [Beaufort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beaufort_County,_South_Carolina "Beaufort County, South Carolina"), [Colleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colleton_County,_South_Carolina "Colleton County, South Carolina"), [Charleston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleston_County,_South_Carolina "Charleston County, South Carolina"), [Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkeley_County,_South_Carolina "Berkeley County, South Carolina"), [Dorchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorchester_County,_South_Carolina "Dorchester County, South Carolina"), [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_County,_South_Carolina "Georgetown County, South Carolina"), and [Horry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horry_County,_South_Carolina "Horry County, South Carolina") counties will go into effect on Monday, September 2, at noon. On September 2, as Dorian's track shifted, a hurricane watch was issued for the entire coast. This was later upgraded to a warning as Dorian's expected track took it near the coast.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

#### North Carolina

On August 30, [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina") governor [Roy Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Cooper "Roy Cooper") declared a state of emergency for the entire state, due to the hurricane.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-108)[Charlotte Motor Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Motor_Speedway "Charlotte Motor Speedway") opened their campgrounds free of charge to evacuees of Hurricane Dorian.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-109) In [Durham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham,_North_Carolina "Durham, North Carolina"), a large statewide hurricane shelter opened inside the former [Sears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sears "Sears") store at the [Northgate Mall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northgate_Mall_(Durham) "Northgate Mall (Durham)").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-110)

The [University of North Carolina at Wilmington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_North_Carolina_at_Wilmington "University of North Carolina at Wilmington") cancelled classes for the week of September 3 and issued a mandatory evacuation of the campus.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-111) Over the Labor Day weekend, several school districts announced plans to close ahead of expected evacuations. [New Hanover County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hanover_County,_North_Carolina "New Hanover County, North Carolina"), [Pender County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pender_County,_North_Carolina "Pender County, North Carolina") and [Brunswick County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunswick_County,_North_Carolina "Brunswick County, North Carolina"), all in the [Cape Fear region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Fear_(region) "Cape Fear (region)"), cancelled public schools on September 4–5, as did several private schools and community colleges.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-112)

Early voting for most counties in the [special election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_North_Carolina's_3rd_congressional_district_special_election "2019 North Carolina's 3rd congressional district special election") in North Carolina's 3rd congressional district and for some counties in the [special election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_North_Carolina's_9th_congressional_district_special_election "2019 North Carolina's 9th congressional district special election") for the 9th congressional district was also temporarily halted after Wednesday, September 4 as a result, until the [North Carolina State Board of Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_State_Board_of_Elections "North Carolina State Board of Elections") could decide what action to take.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-113) Ultimately, Karen Brinson Bell, the Board's Executive Director, would opt to use her emergency powers to extend early voting hours for the 9th district through Saturday, September 7, but only in four harder-hit counties that actually closed polling sites,[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-114) and to have other counties further inland which did not close polling sites[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-115) end early voting on Friday, September 6, as originally prescribed under state law, in order to make the most of the district's resources.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-116) Likewise, the Board extended early voting hours through Saturday for 11 counties[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-117) in the 3rd district, but not for 6 other affected counties [[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-118) suffering from "power outages, poor conditions or a lack of workers."[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-119)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-120)

Further north, along the [Outer Banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_Banks "Outer Banks") in [Dare County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dare_County,_North_Carolina "Dare County, North Carolina") a mandatory evacuation order was given on September 2, 2019. Visitors and tourists were required to evacuate by noon on September 3, while residents were required to evacuate by 6:00 a.m. on September 4.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-121) The state's ports were closed starting at 1:00 p.m. on Wednesday, September 4, until further notice. On September 3, Governor Cooper activated more than 300 members of the [North Carolina National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_National_Guard "North Carolina National Guard") to help aid in recovery efforts.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-122)

On September 3, a hurricane watch was issued for the entire coastline. It was later upgraded to a warning just a few hours later.

#### Virginia

On September 2, [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia") governor [Ralph Northam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Northam "Ralph Northam") declared a state of emergency ahead of Dorian's anticipated impact on coastal Virginia.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-123)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-124)

On September 3, a tropical storm watch was issued for the Delmarva Peninsula. This was upgraded to a warning a day later as Dorian's track became more apparent.

#### Maryland and Delaware

On September 4, as Dorian's large size was expected to potentially bring tropical storm conditions to southern Maryland and Delaware, in correspondence with the upgrading of the tropical storm watch in effect for the Delmarva to a warning, a tropical storm watch was issued for areas south of [Fenwick Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenwick_Island,_Delaware "Fenwick Island, Delaware"), and areas of the Tidal [Potomac River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potomac_River "Potomac River") south of [Cobb Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cobb_Island_(Maryland) "Cobb Island (Maryland)"), as well as areas south of [Drum Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_Point,_Maryland "Drum Point, Maryland"). In [Ocean City, Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_City,_Maryland "Ocean City, Maryland"), officials closed the seawall and removed items from the beach and boardwalk; swimming restrictions were also put into place.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-wboc-125)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-wboc2-126) In [Rehoboth Beach, Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rehoboth_Beach,_Delaware "Rehoboth Beach, Delaware"), swimming restrictions were also put into place, while the portion of the weekend Sandcastle Contest to take place on September 6 was cancelled.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-wboc2-126)[Larry Hogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Hogan "Larry Hogan") also authorized Maryland's Helicopter Aquatic Rescue Team to help with the North Carolina rescue.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-127)

As Dorian was pulled to the northeast by a passing [cold front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_front "Cold front"), the storm passed just 150 miles (240 km) offshore of New England. As a result of this near-miss, a tropical storm watch was issued on September 5 from [Woods Hole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woods_Hole,_Massachusetts "Woods Hole, Massachusetts") to [Sagamore Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagamore_Beach,_Massachusetts "Sagamore Beach, Massachusetts"), including [Nantucket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nantucket "Nantucket") and [Martha's Vineyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha's_Vineyard "Martha's Vineyard"), in [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts"). On September 6, a tropical storm warning was issued for the northern coast of [Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine "Maine") from [Bar Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_Harbor,_Maine "Bar Harbor, Maine") to [Eastport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastport,_Maine "Eastport, Maine").

#### Elsewhere

In [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee"), [Bristol Motor Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_Motor_Speedway "Bristol Motor Speedway") opened one of their campgrounds free of charge to evacuees of Hurricane Dorian.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-128) Along the [Jersey Shore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey_Shore "Jersey Shore") in [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey"), officials in [Margate City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margate_City,_New_Jersey "Margate City, New Jersey") prepared sandbags in case of flooding from the storm while officials in [Brigantine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigantine,_New_Jersey "Brigantine, New Jersey") removed lifeguard stands and boats from the beach.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-129)

In advance of Dorian, [Airbnb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbnb "Airbnb") offered free housing to evacuees in Florida, Georgia, Alabama, and the Carolinas, valid from August 31 through September 16.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-130) AT&T, Verizon, Sprint, and T-Mobile waived charges and/or provided unlimited data to customers within affected states.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-131) The American Red Cross Utah Region deployed members to the Southeast U.S.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-132) For days in advance of the storm, experts at U.S. Geological Survey warned of the likelihood of [rip currents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rip_current "Rip current") and [beach erosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beach_erosion "Beach erosion") along the Southeast U.S. shoreline.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-133) The organization deployed at least 150 storm-tide sensors and 22 other instruments to track the hurricane's effects along the coast.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-134)

#### Alabama controversy

Main article: [Hurricane Dorian–Alabama controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian%E2%80%93Alabama_controversy "Hurricane Dorian–Alabama controversy")

See also: [False or misleading statements by Donald Trump §Hurricane Dorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/False_or_misleading_statements_by_Donald_Trump#Hurricane_Dorian "False or misleading statements by Donald Trump")

On September 1, President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") tweeted that multiple states, including [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama "Alabama"), "will most likely be hit (much) harder than anticipated."[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-2019-09-01_DJT-135) By that date, no weather forecaster was predicting that Dorian would impact Alabama, and the eight National Hurricane Center forecast updates over the preceding 24 hours showed Dorian steering well away from Alabama and moving up the Atlantic coast.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Embury-136)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-137) Trump was apparently relying on information that was several days old.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-138) Twenty minutes later, the [Birmingham, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham,_Alabama "Birmingham, Alabama") office of the [National Weather Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Weather_Service "National Weather Service") (NWS) issued a tweet that appeared to contradict Trump, saying that Alabama "will NOT see any impacts from Dorian".[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-2019-09-01_NWS-139) Over the following days Trump insisted repeatedly that he had been right about the hurricane threatening Alabama.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-140)

[Video 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/20/President_Trump_Receives_a_Hurricane_Dorian_Update.webm?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=rest&utm_content=original)

President Trump displays the altered map in a video published by the White House on September 4, 2019.

On September 4 in the Oval Office, Trump displayed a modified version of the National Hurricane Center's August 29 diagram of Dorian's projected track. The modification was done with a black [Sharpie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharpie_(marker) "Sharpie (marker)") marker to extend the cone of uncertainty of the hurricane's possible path into southern Alabama.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-guardian-141)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Cappucci-142) Trump said he did not know how the map came to be modified.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-143) The incident resulted in the hashtag "Sharpiegate" trending on Twitter.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-memes-144) Later the same day, Trump tweeted a map dated August 28, showing numerous projected paths of Dorian. Trump falsely asserted "almost all models" showed Dorian hitting Alabama, even though the map showed most predicted paths would not enter Alabama.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Embury-136)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Naylor-145)

On September 6, [NOAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOAA "NOAA") published an unsigned statement which supported Trump's initial claim that Alabama was a target of the storm and criticized the Birmingham NWS office for denying it.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-146)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-guardian-7sep2019-147) It was later revealed that NOAA had been ordered to issue such a statement by [Commerce Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commerce_Secretary "Commerce Secretary")[Wilbur Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilbur_Ross "Wilbur Ross"),[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-NYTthreatened-148) and that he had been told by Acting White House Chief of Staff [Mick Mulvaney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Mulvaney "Mick Mulvaney") to get NOAA to support Trump's original statement that Alabama was threatened.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-149)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-150) This direct White House involvement raised questions about political influence over NOAA, and is under investigation by multiple agencies including NOAA's acting chief scientist, the inspector general of the Commerce Department, and the House of Representatives committee which oversees NOAA.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-NYTthreatened-148)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Budryk-151)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-WaPo-152)

### Atlantic Canada

Main article: [Effects of Hurricane Dorian on Atlantic Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effects_of_Hurricane_Dorian_on_Atlantic_Canada "Effects of Hurricane Dorian on Atlantic Canada")

As Dorian approached [Atlantic Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Canada "Atlantic Canada"), hurricane and tropical storm warnings were issued for [Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Scotia "Nova Scotia"), [Prince Edward Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Edward_Island "Prince Edward Island"), and [Newfoundland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newfoundland "Newfoundland").[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-153) On September 6, the Halifax Regional Municipality encouraged residents living along the eastern shores of Nova Scotia to evacuate, citing expected high winds, heavy rainfall, and waves up to 15 m (49 ft) in height.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-154) The Nova Scotia Emergency Management Office implored residents to secure easily dislodged objects to prevent high winds from turning them into projectiles, drawing comparisons to [Hurricane Juan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Juan "Hurricane Juan") in 2003.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-155)[Nova Scotia Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Scotia_Power "Nova Scotia Power") set up an emergency operations center and mobilized 1,000 personnel, including forestry crews, damage assessors, as well as power line technicians from adjacent provinces, to prepare for Dorian's impacts.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-156)[WestJet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WestJet "WestJet"), [Air Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Canada "Air Canada"), and [Porter Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porter_Airlines "Porter Airlines") issued travel advisories for the weekend and waived rebooking fees for flights to and from affected areas.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-157)

Increased tides were experienced in The Bahamas ahead of the storm, with [rip currents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rip_current "Rip current") occurring as well. On September 1, 2019, hurricane conditions arrived in some of the [Abaco Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abaco_Islands "Abaco Islands"). A few hours later, destructive conditions arrived, with Hurricane Dorian making landfall as a Category 5 hurricane at 16:40 UTC, becoming the strongest hurricane in modern records to strike the northwestern Bahamas.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-NHC_01/09/2019-27) Around 12:30 pm AST, Category 5 winds arrived at The Bahamas with the [eyewall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyewall "Eyewall"). Gusts of over 200 mph (320 km/h) also occurred. Devastating storm surge of up to 23 feet swept away many buildings and submerged a large part of the affected areas.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-177) At 7:00 (UTC) on September 2, 2019, [Grand Bahama International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Bahama_International_Airport "Grand Bahama International Airport") was underwater.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-178) Minister of Agriculture Michael Pintard reported an estimated [storm tide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storm_tide "Storm tide") of 20 to 25 ft (6.1 to 7.6 m) at his home on Grand Bahama.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-179) The Bahamas prime minister, Hubert Minnis, said "This is a deadly [...] monster storm".[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-180)

[Marsh Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsh_Harbour "Marsh Harbour") received "catastrophic damage", according to an [ABC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(United_States) "ABC News (United States)") team.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-hell-181) Over 75% of the homes had been damaged,[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-182)[Marsh Harbour International Airport's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsh_Harbour_Airport "Marsh Harbour Airport") runway was underwater,[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-183) there was significant flooding on streets and beaches, damage to trees and with some home's roofs ripped off entirely.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-184) The scene was described by an ABC reporter as "pure hell".[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-hell-181) An eight-year-old boy drowned in the storm surge, while the boy's sister was also reported to be missing.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-185)[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-186) Four other people, along with the eight-year-old boy, were confirmed dead on the Abaco Islands, the prime minister told reporters on Monday.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-5_dead_on_Abaco-187)[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-188) By Wednesday, the death toll had been raised to twenty, according to the prime minister.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Bahamas_death_toll_20-189)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Death_toll_20-190) This soon increased to forty-three by Saturday. However, a Bahamas newspaper suggested that the actual death toll could be over 3,000.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-death_toll_rises-191)

The local animal shelters were hit hard by the storm with the Humane Society of Grand Bahama's experiencing stronger storm surges than expected. Workers had attempted to help the animals before retreating to the attic crawl space but almost half of the 190 dogs in their care died in the flooding and some of the 85 cats died as well.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-192) The numbers of animals has varied with earlier reports claiming that there were 135 dogs and 155 cats in the shelters care, with 80 cats and 90 dogs surviving.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-193)

It is feared that the [Bahama nuthatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahama_nuthatch "Bahama nuthatch") may have been wiped out by Dorian, as it caused catastrophic damage to the [Bahamian pineyards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahamian_pineyards "Bahamian pineyards").[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-Critically-194) A 2020 post-hurricane assessment by the [IUCN Red List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IUCN_Red_List "IUCN Red List") still entertains the probability of the species being extant, although likely having a maximum population size of only 50 individuals and likely well below that, and indicates that extensive surveys for the species will be needed to confirm its status.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian#cite_note-195)
